clue.text: Instrumentalist who picked pickled pepper

parts.note: the tongue-twister about a peck of pickled pepper names its picker, whose surname is also a player of pipes

explanation.surface: A nursery tongue-twister's hero, recast as a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: The tongue-twister begins 'Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled pepper'; his surname also means a musician who plays the pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of bagpipes or a pipe is a musician, and the rhyme's pepper-picker bears that surname.

clue.text: Foolish fancy of the sleeping smoker?

definitions.text: Foolish fancy of the sleeping smoker?

parts.words: Foolish fancy of the sleeping smoker?
parts.note: a smoker asleep might well see tobacco equipment in a vision, while the phrase means an unrealistic hope

explanation.surface: A dozing smoker's nighttime vision is dismissed as silly.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for a hopeless fantasy is said to come from opium smoking, so the question mark invites the literal picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An idle fantasy unlikely ever to come true is the idiom's meaning; literally, a vision of a smoking implement.

clue.text: Assuming it's what a green is for

definitions.meaning: assuming as in adopting a false manner or pretending, as one does with airs
on a golf course the green is the area where players tap the ball towards the hole

explanation.surface: Someone presumes to explain the purpose of a golf green.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretending or affecting is one sense; the other is the golf stroke played on the green, with 'on' saying where.

clue.text: Such beef is remarkably good

definitions.meaning: beef cooked only briefly, still red inside
uncommonly fine, as in a treat seldom found

explanation.surface: A diner praises a steak cooked to perfection.
explanation.definitionFit: Underdone meat is one sense; unusual excellence (a rare talent) is the other.

clue.text: Romantic union in which neither scores off the other

definitions.meaning: a marriage made for affection rather than money

definitions.text: in which neither scores off the other
definitions.meaning: in tennis the word for zero is love, so a game where neither player scores is literally a love contest

explanation.surface: A happy couple who never try to get one over on each other.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis, 'love' means a score of nil.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage based on affection is one sense; read as tennis, a game where both scores stay at nil.

clue.text: What the aspiring campanologist must do to become proficient

definitions.text: What the aspiring campanologist must do to become proficient

parts.words: What the aspiring campanologist must do to become proficient
parts.note: a would-be bell-ringer literally has to master the cords that swing the bells, while the idiom means getting to know how things are done

explanation.surface: Advice for a beginner bell-ringer on reaching competence.
explanation.walkthrough: A campanologist is a bell-ringer; church bells are rung by pulling ropes, so the idiom for mastering a job becomes literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to master the basic procedures of a job, here taken literally for someone pulling bell cords.

clue.text: Made mulled drink

indicators.note: mulled wine is heated and stirred with spices, so the word signals the letters before it being mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone brewed a warm spiced beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mulled' looks like part of the drink's description but rearranges MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an alcoholic beverage made from fermented honey and water.

clue.text: Move to beat in dance

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
go means move, as in 'make a move'

explanation.surface: A dancer is told to step in time with the rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' suggests musical rhythm, fitting the dance, but here it means to thrash; 'to' sets the move after the beating.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Latin American ballroom dance originating in Argentina.

clue.text: Robust Victorian novelist

definitions.meaning: sturdy and able to endure harsh conditions
Thomas, author of Tess of the d'Urbervilles

explanation.surface: Praise for a vigorous nineteenth-century author.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough and resilient is one sense; Thomas, the writer of Far from the Madding Crowd, is the other.

clue.text: Simple apostle

parts.note: the fisherman disciple, also called Simon, was a plain unlettered man

explanation.surface: A humble follower of Jesus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simple' nods to Simon, this apostle's other name, as well as to his humble fisherman's life.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief of the twelve disciples, a Galilean fisherman, bore this name, given him by Jesus.

clue.text: He casts no vote for the consumption of alcohol

definitions.text: He casts no vote for the consumption of alcohol

parts.words: He casts no vote for the consumption of alcohol
parts.note: read one way a voter who sits out a ballot, read another a teetotaller who is no supporter of drinking

explanation.surface: A voter refuses to back the drinking lobby.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a ballot on licensing laws; the word covers both a voter who declines to vote and a person who never drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller refrains from drink, and someone who declines to vote in a ballot also refrains, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Novel extract about a Frenchman having a rough ride

indicators.note: the word for a novel is placed around the Frenchman, so 'about' signals one piece wrapping another

parts.note: a novel is a story
M is the abbreviation for monsieur, a French gentleman
a passage is an extract from a book

explanation.surface: A piece from a book describing a French traveller's bumpy journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts M (Monsieur) inside STORY to give STORMY. 'Novel extract' looks like one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbulent sea crossing, or figuratively a difficult time, is a hard and bumpy journey.

clue.text: It's a bit wet-and so is he

definitions.meaning: a single falling droplet of water
a feeble, wet person is called by the same word

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a thing is damp, and so is the man beside it.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'wet' means feeble, so a wet person is called a drip.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling drop of liquid is one sense; a spineless, insipid person is the British slang other.

clue.text: Order son to take work as a private eye, maybe

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A father tells his son to take a job as a detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command to the son, but it rearranges SON to SNO; 'to take' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective pries into others' affairs, and a prying investigator is one example of a person who does so.

clue.text: It sounds as if it's wholly sacred

indicators.note: the clue says the word that follows is heard rather than read, so its spoken form is wanted

parts.note: completely, said out loud with a silent w

explanation.surface: Something completely sacred is described twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Blessed or consecrated things are dedicated to God, which is the meaning here.

clue.text: It's exactly what gluttonous taxidermists do

definitions.text: It's exactly what gluttonous taxidermists do

parts.words: It's exactly what gluttonous taxidermists do
parts.note: greedy eaters cram food into themselves and taxidermists fill animal skins, one verb covering both

explanation.surface: Greedy animal preservers do something in two ways at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Taxidermists fill the skins of dead animals; gluttons fill themselves with food: one verb does both.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluttons cram themselves with food, and taxidermists fill skins with padding: a single verb for both.

clue.text: They employ you and me with many a hesitation

parts.note: we are us
er is a sound of hesitation, and several of them are ers

explanation.surface: Bosses who keep hesitating over hiring us.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opening two words, not a description of employers.
explanation.definitionFit: People who make use of something are its consumers, so those who employ a tool are this.

clue.text: Hear the news and cotton on

definitions.meaning: receive a communication or report
British idiom for finally understanding

explanation.surface: Someone learns some news and understands it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cotton on' is British for 'realise'.
explanation.definitionFit: Receiving a communication is one sense; finally grasping an implied point is the idiomatic other.

clue.text: May not men change in an instant?

indicators.note: the letters are made to alter their order, as a change of arrangement

explanation.surface: A question whether men could alter their ways suddenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges MAYNOTMEN; the surface question makes 'change' look like a verb about men.
explanation.definitionFit: Very soon, at any second now, is the meaning of the phrase.

clue.text: Regards exercise as injurious to one's view ofthings

parts.note: to regard is to look at, as eyes do
to train is to exercise

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a workout damages how one sees the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ofthings' is a run-together printing of 'of things'. 'as' joins; the definition is loose, describing what harms sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiredness of sight from overuse damages one's vision, which is a person's literal view of things.

clue.text: Galsworthy's landowner?

parts.note: the first novel of the Forsyte Saga by John Galsworthy has a title meaning a possessor of estates

explanation.surface: A question about a landed character in a famous novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The first Forsyte Saga novel (1906) by John Galsworthy carries this title; Soames Forsyte is its possessive hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy owner of estates is literally one with possessions, and Galsworthy's novel title names such a person.

clue.text: Team which is neither at the top nor the bottom

definitions.meaning: a sports eleven or squad

definitions.text: neither at the top nor the bottom
definitions.meaning: a flank or surface that is not upper nor lower

explanation.surface: A team stuck in mid-table, never top nor bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports team is one sense; a lateral face of an object, between top and base, is the other.

clue.text: Commence Strategic Arms Reduction Talks

definitions.meaning: begin
the US-Soviet nuclear negotiations, known by their initials

explanation.surface: An order to open disarmament negotiations.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin is one sense; the acronym of the Cold War nuclear treaty talks is the other.

clue.text: Wee whisky taken before a theatrical performance

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of whisky, especially in Scotland

explanation.surface: A small Scotch before going to see a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken before' just joins; DRAM comes before A.
explanation.definitionFit: A play performed on stage is the basic sense of the word.

clue.text: A pious demand for silence is foolish

parts.note: pi is informal short for pious
sh is said to call for quiet

explanation.surface: A devout person's call for quiet is called silly.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is a dated British shortening of 'pious'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting like an ape means behaving in a silly, imitative way.

clue.text: A great many people entertain

definitions.meaning: a multitude or throng
to receive guests and look after them

explanation.surface: Crowds are being given a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A multitude is one sense; acting as a party-giver for guests is the other.

clue.text: Not in favour of setting a trap

parts.note: a gin is a snare for catching game

explanation.surface: Someone opposes the laying of snares.
explanation.walkthrough: AGIN is dialect for 'against'; 'setting' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: It is dialect for opposed or against.

clue.text: Attempt to inflict a wound with a knife

definitions.meaning: a try, as in 'have a go'

definitions.text: inflict a wound with a knife
definitions.meaning: to thrust a blade into someone

explanation.surface: A would-be assassin tries to knife someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A try at something is one sense; thrusting a blade into someone is the other.

clue.text: Brewed ales again provide re lief from pain

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients up, so the letters of the following words are mixed

explanation.surface: Beer made a second time eases a hangover.
explanation.walkthrough: 're lief' is 'relief' split in printing. 'Brewed' rearranges ALESAGAIN; 'provide' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Medically, it is the absence of sensation of pain, so it means relief from suffering.

clue.text: Letter from Greece containing the briefest expression of grate, tude

parts.note: ta is a very short British way of saying thank you

explanation.surface: A Greek pen-friend sends a very short thank-you note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grate, tude' is 'gratitude' broken in printing; the British say 'ta' for thanks. 'containing' only links: the Greek letter contains the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Fair rate set about the first of November for the cost of travel

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the next piece, so 'about' signals wrapping
to set something is to arrange it, so the letters before are reordered
only the opening letter of the following word is wanted

explanation.surface: A reasonable price has been fixed for November travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges FAIRRATE, and 'about' places that around N, the first of November.
explanation.definitionFit: The price paid for a rail ticket is a charge for a journey.

clue.text: Staff receive instruction to continue playing cricket

definitions.meaning: a short stick or rod, as a conductor or relay runner holds
in cricket a batsman told to keep batting is told to carry on at the crease

explanation.surface: Ground staff are told to keep the match going.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, 'bat on' tells a cricketer to keep batting; 'receive' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod such as a conductor or relay runner holds is one sense; 'bat on' as two words is the cricket order.
